requirement: Desktop release notes come from one docs changelog page: prepare reads it at the release sha, publish waits for the docs host (which serves the page as raw markdown too), each build carries its own notes

oracle.invariant: S1: a minor release ships the page's Highlights, a patch its own ## X.Y.Z section without the 'Released' line; a page of another minor, a missing or empty section give no notes; a line naming a third party ('Bump dsh-passwords 2.7.7') or not in English, front matter without slug changelog/desktop/X.Y or with an unquoted version, more than 5 Highlights are problems; the draft never overwrites a page or section without --force; bundle notes are release-notes.txt + release-notes.json { version, page, docsOrigin }. S2: stable prepare without the page section for its version (no page, no ## X.Y.Z, a page with 'Bump dsh-passwords') is refused before checkout and build, naming file and section; --notes is refused for stable; a dev build warns and ships the PR notes; the manifest records notes.source 'docs changelog/desktop/X.Y.md#<section>@<sha>' and notes.contentSha256; the build gets the frozen notes; stable publish is refused with 'deploy docs first' when the docs host does not answer 200 for /changelog/desktop/X.Y/ and X.Y.md or serves another text, with nothing written; --skip-docs-check is refused for stable; a real store refuses another docs origin than its channel's. S3: every committed page passes; a copy with 'Bump dsh-passwords 2.7.7' fails. S4: the build writes changelog/desktop/X.Y.md for every X.Y.md page and nothing else, without front matter, the rest verbatim with its _(Desktop only)_ badges; the release tooling reads the same notes for every version from the copy as from the page; publish's docs check accepts a host serving the copy and names the .md when it is missing; the docs host answers /changelog/desktop/0.5.md with 200 text/markdown; charset=utf-8 and cache-control no-cache.
oracle.productSourcesScope: file-level: the files the case imports, reads or runs (declaration line, or the first code line); the invariant is exercised through them, the executed assertion is the case command
